h1: The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho — Where You Open the Curtains to a Sea of Mist Above Rattanai Reservoir
intro: The selling point here is what sits right outside your room. The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho is laid out along a ridge that faces the valley and Rattanai Reservoir, so almost every room opens its curtains in the morning to a sea of mist drifting over the water. You can choose a private cabin for 2-6 guests or an air-conditioned VIP tent that still sleeps comfortably, and dinner is a shared moo kratha / BBQ over the cool mountain air. From approx. ฿2,200/night. Score 8.7 from 42 reviews.

body.html: The Proud Resort sits at Ban Kanok-ngam in Khao Kho sub-district, Khao Kho, Phetchabun. What gets it talked about is the layout: it is built along a ridge that faces the valley and Rattanai Reservoir, so almost every room looks straight out onto the mountains and the water. In the late-rainy to cool season a sea of mist forms over the reservoir at dawn, and that is the picture most guests come here to catch.

Accommodation comes in two main forms. Private cabins sleep anywhere from 2 to 6 guests, decorated in a clean modern style with air-con, TV, fridge, hot water and a balcony to sit and take in the view. The other option is an air-conditioned VIP tent for 2-4 guests, fully kitted out like a normal room, ideal for travellers who want the camping feel without roughing it. Many guests note the rooms are clean, feel new, and that the view really does match the photos.
"I woke up, opened the door, and there was mist filling the reservoir right in front of me — no need to go anywhere, just sit with a coffee at the room and watch it all morning."

On food, the resort offers a buffet breakfast (charged separately) and a moo kratha / BBQ dinner you can order and share as a group, which suits the cool Khao Kho air nicely. The overall mood leans toward privacy and quiet — better for couples, families or groups of friends who want to relax with the view than for anyone after on-site entertainment. There is free Wi-Fi and free parking by the cabins.

The location is in the inner Khao Kho area. It is a short drive to Khao Kho Viewpoint, the Khao Kho Royal Palace and the wind-farm fields, while Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaew and the Kanchanaphisek pagoda can be folded into the same trip. The owner is regularly praised in reviews for being warm and helpful, happy to suggest routes around Khao Kho. The resort also holds a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice award (top 10% of properties) and a Booking.com score around 8.5.

To be straight with you, the thing to set expectations on is that the real appeal here is the view and the quiet, not lavish facilities. There is no swimming pool or big cafe like the heavily themed resorts, and the on-site food choice is limited — if you want variety you will need to drive out. The road up Khao Kho is steep and winding in places, so check your vehicle and drive carefully. But if what you are after is waking up to a sea of mist outside your door at a price you can actually justify, this place delivers exactly that.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: for peak mist, come between October and February and book several weeks ahead, because the best-view cabins and VIP tents fill fast in the cool season and on long weekends. When you book, ask which rooms face Rattanai Reservoir head-on for the fullest view. Pack warm layers — early mornings on Khao Kho really are cold — and wake up early to catch the mist before the sun burns it off.

honestSummary: The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho is best for travellers chasing a sea of mist right outside the room and peace and quiet on Khao Kho at a fair price — its strength is the ridge-top location facing Rattanai Reservoir, with both private cabins and air-conditioned VIP tents. Just accept that facilities are modest and the mist depends on the weather of the day.
honestChecks: If you want a resort packed with a pool and on-site activities — this place is about the view and the quiet, with no pool and not the full facility set of a large resort → if you plan to spend all day inside the resort, a heavily themed one suits better
If you are coming specifically for the sea of mist — mist depends on the weather and is not guaranteed daily → come October-February, wake at dawn, and accept some mornings may be thin or clear

If you have elderly travellers or aren't confident on mountain roads — some cabins are up the slope and the Khao Kho road is steep in parts → ask for an easy-access cabin when booking and check your vehicle before the climb

faqTitle: FAQ — The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho

faq.q: Where is The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 324 Moo 1, Ban Kanok-ngam, Khao Kho sub-district, Khao Kho, Phetchabun, on a ridge facing Rattanai Reservoir. It's about a 15-minute drive to Khao Kho Viewpoint and the Royal Palace, around 20 minutes to the wind farm, roughly 30 minutes to Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaew, and about an hour from Phetchabun town.

faq.q: What does The Proud Resort cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿2,200/night for a private cabin for 2. There are cabins for 2-6 guests and air-conditioned VIP tents for 2-4 that give the camping feel while still sleeping comfortably. Prices vary by cabin size and season — winter and long weekends rise noticeably, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is The Proud Resort best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples, families and groups of friends who want a sea-of-mist view outside the room and a quiet, private mood — more about sitting with a coffee, watching the view and sharing a moo kratha in the cool air than chasing on-site facilities.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit, and will I see the sea of mist?
faq.a: The best window is October to February, when it's cool and mist forms over Rattanai Reservoir often. Waking before sunrise gives the best chance of a full view. That said, the mist depends on the weather each day and isn't guaranteed every morning.

faq.q: What are the VIP tents like?
faq.a: The VIP tents sleep 2-4 guests and are air-conditioned, with a TV, fridge and a view balcony. They give a camping feel up on Khao Kho while still sleeping as comfortably as a normal room — good for anyone who wants to try a tent without bringing their own gear.

faq.q: Does the resort serve food, or do I need to eat out?
faq.a: It offers a buffet breakfast (charged separately) and a moo kratha / BBQ dinner you can order and share as a group. On-site choice is limited, though, so for more variety it's worth driving out to restaurants around the Khao Kho area.
